text: Q5 as SPEC'd wants invariant zeros from the Rosenbrock QZ, a structure-respecting route that never forms Pi_c M. At production the pencil is 4762x4762 and QZ is O(30 n^3). If it is affordable, the diag(Schur(Lred)) spectrum and the QZ zeros are two routes to the same set and their DISAGREEMENT is the conditioning measurement the premortem demands. The structure-respecting route is the SPARSE descriptor pencil spectrum.py already certified: (J - sigma E)^-1 E v = theta v, lambda = sigma + 1/theta, one SuperLU plus Arnoldi, with the index-2 infinities parked at theta=0 where 'largest |theta|' discards them. Cost 21 s LU + 14 s Arnoldi at root A (N=7670), 56 s + 20 s at root B (N=10262) -- two orders cheaper than QZ. With shift sigma=+0.5 (in the RHP, far from all spectrum) it agrees with diag(Schur(Lred)) on the four rightmost eigenvalues to 1.28e-09 (A) and 7.17e-09 (B). A shift placed ON the eigenvalue (-0.3+0.2j) degrades to ~5e-06 because the shifted matrix is then near-singular -- so the RHP shift is the right one, and it is also the one that would have FOUND an RHP eigenvalue first had any existed. It found none.

SIDE-DISCOVERY from the battery: refining the inner/mid panels (16,40)->(20,48) at eps_b=1e-4 moved h_id from -1.06e-3 to +1.56e-4: a 7x shrink AND a sign crossing. FARFIELD EVIDENCE REPAIR (farfield lens, not refuted, minor): kappa=1 is CONFIRMED pointwise (1.000 +- 0.001 on 30/35 betas, rms 5.7e-6 at the wall column) but two of MY evidentiary steps were defective: (1) 'forcing exponentially subleading' is false at window entry, the forcing/orphan crossover sits at xi* = 7.6 INSIDE the fit window, separation >= 10x only for xi >= 17.5; (2) the quoted envelope slope -0.0548 is non-discriminating (a pure power fits the A-envelope BETTER, BIC -265 vs -238) because the envelope argmax sits at the near-axis columns j=31-32 where the correction amplitude c(beta) reaches -6.9 and the fit degrades. The DISCRIMINATING diagnostics are the local slope-product climbing 0.23->0.992 and pointwise interior-beta fits. Also sharpened: sigma=0 is an eigen-consistency statement holding for ANY pure-log field with a self-consistent (alpha,cl,cw) triple (the pre-Newton seed passes with its own weights); the falsifiable content is at O(1/xi). Surviving form: A = (f(beta)/xi)(1 + c(beta)*rho^alpha + ...), c from +0.007 wall-side to -6.9 near-axis.

C1's corner action is a GAUGE RENORMALIZATION: WX -> WX - 6*tau*c at corner order 1, the order where alpha is first selected (order 0 closes as h_id = 0 identically and is alpha-blind). Consequences: (a) any wall-layer-windowed 3D readout is essentially a pure-C1 measurement of gauge-constant motion, not of alpha; (b) h_id's 3D analogue is NOT h_id with the same constants -- the corner identity itself moves with tau; (c) this couples directly to #30 (h2 derivation): the next-order corner identity in 3D must carry the -6c correction. Feeds the 3D program and the h2 work.

FOUR ORDERING BETS, pre-registered by the trajectory pass as the tangent's only surviving forward tests (the axes themselves are ledger-derived; the bet is that the named axis bites FIRST): #30 h2 will first fail via corner-ODE self-annihilation or gauge-variance (pin/gauge direction, #12/#14/#42) before any algebra error; #31 march-vs-exp(tL) disagreement will first be attributed to the pin-deleted perturbation subspace (#13/#14) before any E-not-identity correction; #33 a fixed-grid fold will first fail eps_b/panel replication (#40 signature) before any other failure; #38 a pure radial two-region matching will first fail on the beta axis log-layer (#41, event-307 measurement). CORRECTION to #46 (operator flagged; self-audited): (a) my max_writes=10000 on the snapshot handler was wrong -- one fragile giant file; set to 50 so the series rolls into complete files (extractor already globs+sorts). DISCIPLINE STOP (self-imposed): I am on my third window rule in one hour, which is exactly tension #45 axis 3's hazard. Tuning rule #4 against 3D data would be FITTING THE ANSWER, because 3D has no known answer. RULE: the window rule is CALIBRATED on the 2D control against its OWN known value alpha = -0.34240, FROZEN, then applied unchanged to 3D. No 3D alpha is quotable until the rule is frozen on the control. Control 512^2 at t=1.96/2.44, sup|grad b| 1.05e+04, Casimir 2.3e-10.

The result is a clean negative: no window rule calibrates because the observable has no stationary value in time. Had I tuned rule #4 against 3D data as the momentum wanted, I would have selected a window and a time that produced a plausible number with nothing behind it.

text: OWN 3D LADDER, rungs 1-2 (explicit provenance ic_power=4 zpow=1 r0=0.4 A=100, both this session): N128x384 trust t<=0.003516 sup|w1| x1155.6 cas 2.76e-08 38s; N256x768 trust t<=0.003515 sup|w1| x1443.3 cas 7.16e-09 177s. Trust times agree to 4 digits; AMPLIFICATION differs 25 percent -- not resolution-converged. outcome: OWN 3D LADDER COMPLETE, 3 rungs, full provenance. sup|w1| amplification x1155.6 / x1443.3 / x1803.9; ratios 1.2490 and 1.2499 -- CONSTANT to four digits across two doublings, i.e. a clean power law in grid spacing with NO convergence. Casimir improves 2.76e-8 -> 7.16e-9 -> 1.92e-9 (3.7x per doubling), so the equations are being solved correctly and it is the peak-vorticity OBSERVABLE that is grid-limited. text: CONTROL RUN did not reproduce the archived N256 blowup character: ours peaks sup|grad b| ~6.8e4 near t=2.07 then FALLS to 2.8e4 by t=2.37 with b2_drift degrading 2.3e-10 -> 3.5e-7; archived N256 reports gb_ratio 2219 accel 2.85 to t_trust_end 2.421. Until this is settled the control cannot calibrate anything even with a fixed observable.

CANDIDATE REPLACEMENT OBSERVABLE (do NOT quote yet): the ladder exponent may encode alpha directly. If the corner profile is Omega ~ rho^alpha and the grid resolves to rho ~ dx, then sup|Omega| ~ dx^alpha and halving dx multiplies amplification by 2^|alpha|. Measured gamma = 0.32124 (rungs stable at 0.32073, 0.32175) vs |alpha_2D| = 0.34240: 6.18 percent low. This would BYPASS the broken spatial-window instrument entirely -- no self-similar window in space needs to be found, only a resolution ladder. UNKNOWNS BEFORE IT MEANS ANYTHING: (1) 3 rungs only, and gamma is drifting UP between them (0.32073 -> 0.32175), so it may not be converged either; (2) the derivation assumes the grid cutoff sits inside the self-similar regime, unverified; (3) this is a 3D run and alpha_3D should differ from alpha_2D by exactly the drift we are trying to measure, so 6.18 percent may be signal, artifact, or both; (4) needs the identical ladder on the 2D CONTROL, where the answer is known, before any 3D number is credible.

ANISOTROPY (new, measured, nothing in the record names it): the 3D corner layer aspect ratio ell_z/ell_r moves monotonically 2.96 -> 0.06 over t=0.002922..0.003499 on N256x768 (factor 50), because ell_z collapses like (ts-t)^1.32 while ell_r GROWS 2.9x. N128 shows the same sign. BOTH load-bearing constructions presuppose a constant ratio: the polar corner profile uses ONE rho and ONE alpha, and alpha_eff fits isotropic shells. If the ratio keeps sliding, alpha_eff(t) is a moving mixture of two exponents and its drift is nonzero for reasons unrelated to the 3D corrections -- i.e. the drift measurement is confounded at the root.

3D ARGMAX DETACHES FROM THE WALL RING late in the run (measured N256x768): wall-distance 1-r* is 6.27e-7 through t=0.0032, then 1.76e-3 at t=0.0034 and 2.81e-3 at t=0.0035; N128 gives 3.07e-3 and 4.21e-3 (33 percent larger, so refinement shrinks but does not kill it). The campaign's OWN rule (DEGENERACY_LATTICE.md) says an off-ring argmax means a DIFFERENT STAGE, not the target singularity -- it is how the Boussinesq s=4 case was disqualified. Detachment begins exactly in the last third, the only part with self-similar signal. The 2D control's peak stays pinned to the wall throughout, so this is 3D-specific.
outcome: G1 SETTLES IT IN THE GOOD DIRECTION: the 3D argmax wall-detachment is a CONVERGING ARTIFACT, not physical off-ring drift. Measured at matched tau=(ts-t)/ts across all three own-provenance rungs: gap halves cleanly per doubling -- tau=0.012 gives 4e-3/2e-3/1e-3, tau=0.05 gives 2e-3/1e-3/5e-4, tau=0.20 gives 3e-6/6e-7/2e-7. By the campaign's own DEGENERACY_LATTICE rule an off-ring argmax would mean a DIFFERENT STAGE (how the s=4 Boussinesq case was disqualified); the halving says instead that we ARE on the target singularity and merely cannot resolve it.

text: G1 MODALITY: DECISIVE INCONCLUSIVE. The resolved window and the self-similar window DO NOT OVERLAP. At N512x1536 the thin direction holds >2 cells only for tau >~ 0.1; the self-similar signal lives at tau < 0.05. At the only two tau with two readable rungs the aspect-ratio spread is 0.445 (tau=0.20: 2.357/1.523/1.745) and 0.621 (tau=0.10: 0.525/0.999). Modality (one exponent vs two) CANNOT be read from these runs and it is not a sampling problem -- the mesh floor sits between us and the answer. SHARPENING: the unconverged direction is ell_r, NOT ell_z. At tau=0.10 both N256 and N512 give ell_z ~ 1.3e-3 (2 cells and 4 cells of different size landing on the same physical width), so the entire rung-to-rung ratio difference comes from ell_r. CONSEQUENCE: G2 (half-period Chebyshev-z basis) is a HARD PRECONDITION for reading G1, not an option.
outcome: G1's verdict is now CONFIRMED BY AN INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT. G1 reached it by counting cells across the thin direction (>2 cells only for tau >~ 0.1 at N512). The 3D free residual reaches the same place from unimposed physics: u1 is monotone along the wall line at tau=0.167 on all three rungs (0 breaks) and is a full 2-cell sawtooth by tau=0.007 (break fraction 0.87/0.94/0.97). So the honest 3D trust window is tau >~ 0.17 while the self-similar signal lives at tau < 0.05: THE CLEAN WINDOW AND THE SINGULAR WINDOW DO NOT OVERLAP, established twice by structurally different routes. This is a property of the current z basis, not of the physics -- which is precisely what G2 tests.

text: HONEST TRUST WINDOW for the 2D control is t <~ 1.50, not 2.398. Every march-based number this session was read inside the contaminated region. Re-running G0 restricted to t < 1.5 is the only way to learn whether the spatial-window observable is genuinely dead or was killed by bad data -- but at t < 1.5 the corner is still smooth (slope +1.1, the Taylor regime), so the resolved-and-clean window may be EMPTY. If it is empty, that is the real result: this control cannot certify anything at 512^2, and the calibration arm needs either the G2 basis or a bounds-preserving scheme.

COLLAPSE TEST (scale-map instrument, first run): CONFOUNDED as built, but informative. Low residual is achieved by TWO non-self-similar modes: (a) nothing happening -- 2D control t<1.5 scores 0.044 while the corner is still smooth (slope +1.1, Taylor regime); (b) structure FROZEN at the mesh scale with only amplitude growing -- 3D beyond trust scores 0.035, the BEST of any window, with dlog_rho EXACTLY 0.000. The discriminating requirement is low residual WITH nonzero spatial rescaling, and no window shows one above the 0.025 scan resolution. RESULT DESPITE THE CONFOUND: zero spatial shift at the best-scoring window is an independent confirmation of GRID LOCK -- the structure ceases to rescale and grows in amplitude only. Third structurally-different route to the same conclusion after the G1 cell count and the u1 sawtooth. FIXES NEEDED before re-run: finer shift scan (below 0.025), reject dlog_rho ~ 0 as a null mode, and require the amplitude/scale exponent ratio to be consistent across pairs.
outcome: COLLAPSE v2 (continuous optimiser, distant anchor, null-mode gate |s|>=0.05, residual gate <0.10, a=A/s consistency required): NO COLLAPSE IN ANY WINDOW, including RESOLVED ones. N512 in its own resolved window tau in [0.20,0.33] where gamma~0 confirms the mesh is not the limiter: scale shift s stays -0.005..-0.041 while amplitude shift A reaches -0.54, giving a = A/s ~ 11-13, and rms grows monotonically 0.043 -> 0.453 with anchor distance. The profile is CHANGING SHAPE, not translating: the structure grows in amplitude without rescaling even where fully resolved. Physical reading: at tau ~ 0.3 the flow is simply not self-similar yet -- self-similarity is asymptotic as t->ts. FIFTH independent route to the non-overlap conclusion and the FIRST that measures rescaling directly rather than through a proxy. v1's confound is fully explained: it scored best on frozen data because it lacked the |s| gate. SELF-CRITICISM ON RECORD: the N1024 resolved window holds only 5 snapshots because I set ckpt-sim-dt=2e-4 to conserve disk, which undercut the very measurement the rung was run for (its fit returned rms 2.4). Nothing can be said about tau~0.08 from this data.

A re-run at ckpt-sim-dt 2e-5 over ONLY the late window (resume from checkpoint at t~0.0028, march to 0.003512) would give ~35 snapshots in the resolved band at a fraction of the 5.9h cost. Requires freeing disk first. This is the cheapest available path to testing whether tau~0.08 shows collapse.

DESIGN NOTE for EJA (operator's idea, park for later, do not build now): a PAPER-PLAN operator. Before any compute, write the plan out longhand, derive its numbers on the scratchpad, and read it back as proofreading -- then act. Today it paid immediately: staging the pod plan on paper surfaced that ts was never verified for OUR IC and that all four rungs march PAST the nominal blowup time without blowing up, which would have consumed the entire 92 dollar budget answering the wrong question. Distinct from preflight (which collides against the PAST record) and from the 3-step denotation chain (which checks what an object will DENOTE): paper-plan is about forcing the plan's own arithmetic to exist BEFORE the run, where it can be read and audited. RE-EXAMINATION REQUIRED, scoped honestly. RESOLUTION-CONVERGED-GROWTH TEST, first attempt: FAILS at N128 vs N256, with a caveat that may disqualify N128 rather than the test. Corner-localised observable (|omega1| max over z on the wall column r->1), both runs marched to their own trust ends (0.006789 / 0.006615, cas ~1e-3), 132 snapshots each. Neither rung monotone; negative-rate fraction 28.8 vs 19.6 percent; matched-time relative rate difference median 0.797, mean 1.538, max 18.4. BUT: at N256 the wall-ring value EQUALS the global sup (9.8203e4 both), i.e. the maximum sits ON the wall where the singularity forms, whereas at N128 they differ (2.95e4 vs 4.09e4) and the max is OFF-wall. N128 therefore may not resolve the wall structure at all and should be treated as disqualified rather than as evidence against convergence. DECISIVE TEST IS N256 vs N512, both of which put the max on the wall. Also note the localisation did help: the global sup oscillated -987..3300 while the localised rate is better behaved, but still non-monotone.

N512 GROWTH-CHARACTER RESULT (decisive rung, trust t<=0.006171, cas hit exactly 1.00e-3, amplification x231916): wall==global confirmed (3.637e5 both), matching N256's self-consistency and settling that N128 alone was disqualified for not resolving the wall. N512 IMPROVES in absolute behaviour: 0.0 percent negative-rate fraction over t>0.004 (vs N256's 23.4 percent), i.e. monotone corner growth for the first time at any rung. BUT N256 vs N512 matched-time rates still DISAGREE: median relative diff 0.833, mean 3.29, spikes to 33x at t=0.0055. RESOLUTION-CONVERGED GROWTH CHARACTER IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED. Net verdict: closer, not there. The corner-localised observable is doing its job (each successive rung's raw signal quality visibly improves: N128 off-wall, N256 on-wall but non-monotone, N512 on-wall and monotone) but agreement between the two trustworthy rungs is still absent. Honest reading: EITHER one more resolution doubling (N1024, localised diagnostic, cost ~4x N512's 2.6h) would show N512-vs-N1024 finally agreeing, extending the monotone-improvement trend, OR the disagreement itself is not shrinking with N and something else is at play (e.g. genuinely different transient behaviour per rung, not measurement noise). The N512-vs-N1024 comparison is the next test and it is now well motivated by a real trend rather than a guess.

POD RUN LIVE (RunPod d0dnxx14r737u8, A100 community, $1.39/hr, 256 vCPU). DECISION CHANGED MID-SETUP AND IT WAS THE RIGHT CALL: the plan was resume-from-checkpoint to bank the laptop's 5.5h, but the 1.5GB checkpoint upload failed repeatedly through a flaky proxy (scp connection reset, rsync --append-verify exhausted 20 retries, chunked upload hit my own scp -p/-P option collision). Pivoted to RE-MARCHING FROM t=0 ON THE POD instead, which is FASTER than fighting the upload and eliminates a whole risk class (partial file, version mismatch, resume-path bugs) while yielding a full high-cadence series rather than only the tail. MEASURED: 32 MPI ranks give ~2.7 s/iteration against the laptop's 15.3 s/iteration single-process, a 5.7x speedup (less than the 15x hoped -- 2D-grid communication overhead), and matrix build 3s vs 37s. Config identical provenance: Nz=1024 Nr=3072 A=100 ic_power=4 zpow=1 r0=0.4, tmax=0.0065, ckpt-sim-dt 2e-5, timeout 5h. Live gates sidecar armed (u1 sign principle, wall-column sawtooth fraction, wall==global), writing /workspace/runs/gates.jsonl, failures loud. PRE-REGISTERED ABORT: trust break before t=0.0050 kills the N512-vs-N1024 comparison and IS ITSELF THE FINDING (a closing-trust-window problem no resolution fixes). Extrapolated trust break from the ladder (0.006789/0.006615/0.006171) predicts ~0.0055, INSIDE the comparison window, so this is a live risk not a formality. Cost so far ~$0.55.

POD RUN v2 REQUIREMENTS, derived from the failure: (a) SMOKE TEST FIRST -- one 60-second multi-rank run with the snapshot handler enabled, verifying an actual .h5 write completes, BEFORE launching the long job. (b) Fix the parallel write: either build h5py against MPI-aware HDF5, or set the Dedalus file handler to per-process output (parallel='gather' or virtual-file mode), or run FEWER ranks with snapshots written only by rank 0. (c) WATCHDOG MANDATORY on paid compute: a loop that checks the stream file mtime every N minutes and stops the pod if it stalls or DONE appears. The 7-hour idle burn was not the run failing, it was nobody watching. (d) The gates sidecar must write a heartbeat line even when it finds nothing, so an empty gates.log is distinguishable from a dead sidecar. (e) Reconsider rank count: 32 ranks gave only 5.7x speedup on a 2D grid, and fewer ranks would both reduce contention and cost little speed.

PARALLEL-WRITE BUG FIXED AND VALIDATED LOCALLY (free). Added parallel='gather' to BOTH file handlers in dedalus_axisym.py, guarded so it no-ops at comm.size==1 (single-process laptop path byte-unchanged). VERIFIED: 4-rank mpirun wrote snap_smoke4_s1.h5 with NO lock error, and the physics is bit-identical to the single-process smoke run (sup|w1| x20.3, cas_drift 3.77e-11 in both). The 32-rank pod failure mode is closed. ALSO CORRECTED, on the operator's challenge: the pod's nproc=256 was the HOST core count, not our container's cgroup quota, so 32 ranks may already have been AT or OVER our real allocation -- which would itself explain the weak scaling. My '5.7x speedup' was invalid anyway: it compared 32 pod ranks against the LAPTOP single process, conflating hardware with parallelism. Real quota and a rank-scaling knee must be MEASURED on the next pod (cgroup cpu.max, then 60s runs at 8/16/32/64 ranks) before committing to a rank count. COST NOTE: the A100 pod at 1.39/hr against CPU-only pods capped at 32 vCPU at 0.035/vCPU (=1.12/hr) means a GPU pod is the cheap way to buy cores IF the quota is actually high.

COMPUTE ROUTE DECISION, honest: laptop 8-rank run is LIVE at 13.3 s/it, ETA ~30 hours to trust end, cost zero, parallel-write path exercised and working. Pod alternative: a 32-vCPU CPU pod at cpu5c 0.035/vCPU = 1.12/hr, ~5.6 h, ~6.30 dollars, but must be created in the RunPod console (MCP cannot set vCPU count) and requires a fresh dedalus install since the old volume was deleted. GPU pods are currently unavailable across A100 / RTX5090 / RTX PRO 6000 on community cloud. Credit remaining ~81 dollars. Recommendation: let the laptop run; 30 background hours costs nothing and the result is identical. Spend only if the answer is time-critical.
